title: Ask for a regex, then attack its assumptions
goal: Turn a fuzzy matching request into explicit positive and negative test cases.
explanation: A regex for a limited filter is not a complete email validator. Decide whether a hyphen must occur in the local part or anywhere in the address, whether subdomains count and whether matching is case-insensitive. The activity test runner uses a short-lived worker and synthetic strings, not a production data scan.
sampleInput: Specification: local part must contain a hyphen; domain is one simple label followed by .edu; no spaces; case-insensitive. Match: first-last@example.edu; A-B@COLLEGE.EDU. Reject: firstlast@example.edu; first-last@example.com; firstlast@my-college.edu; first-last@dept.example.edu.
prompt: Propose a bounded JavaScript regex for exactly the stated simplified filter, not RFC-complete email validation. Explain the anchors, local-part hyphen rule, simple domain and case-insensitive flag. Provide results for all supplied tests and at least two edge cases. Do not claim it verifies delivery or institutional status.
workedExample: One limited pattern: ^[A-Z0-9._+]*-[A-Z0-9._+-]*@[A-Z0-9]+(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)*\.edu$ with i flag. Check its actual behaviour; “a-b@example.edu” is a match, while a hyphen only in the domain is insufficient. The simplified grammar intentionally excludes some valid real addresses.

steps.title: Define the policy
steps.text: Write the exact location of the hyphen and domain/subdomain rules before asking for syntax.

steps.title: Get a draft pattern
steps.text: Request the target engine and flags; do not copy syntax intended for a different language.

steps.title: Run the fixture
steps.text: Use the bounded test tool and compare actual results with the reference list.

steps.title: Try edge cases
steps.text: Add spaces, an empty local part and uppercase letters; keep false positives and negatives visible.

steps.title: State the scope
steps.text: Label the filter as a toy policy check, not email validation or proof of eligibility.

checks: All six supplied strings have recorded expected and observed results.
A hyphen only in the domain does not satisfy the local-part requirement.
The report names JavaScript/flags and clearly limits the simplified grammar.
commonMistakes: Calling a matching string a deliverable or institution-verified email address.
Using an unbounded pattern or huge input without a timeout.
offline: Mark expected matches by hand and explain the policy without executing a pattern.

visualSteps.title: Specify
visualSteps.text: Define what counts as a match

reflection: Which valid real-world address might your deliberately simplified filter reject?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. All six supplied strings have recorded expected and observed results.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. A hyphen only in the domain does not satisfy the local-part requirement.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Calling a matching string a deliverable or institution-verified email address.
